results.evidence: Section 3.4: "During the Term, Licensee shall not, and shall procure that its Affiliates do not, license, procure, develop, deploy or use any Competing Product on or in respect of any Vessel. Licensee shall use the Software as its sole solution for the functions described in the definition of Competing Product across all Vessels." Section 1.1 defines "Competing Product" to cover fleet management, voyage optimization, emissions monitoring and reporting, hull, propeller and engine monitoring, and crew management. It defines "Vessel" as any vessel "owned, chartered, managed or operated by Licensee or any Affiliate of Licensee, wherever located in the world". Term Sheet 7.1 says exclusivity covers "voyage-optimization software only, for dry-bulk vessels owned by Nipusk."
results.reason: The covenant binds Nipusk, the client, and goes well beyond the agreed term sheet scope. It covers five function categories rather than one, applies to chartered-in and managed tonnage and Affiliates rather than only owned dry-bulk vessels, and makes TideRoute the 'sole solution' for crew management. TideRoute does not even offer a crew-management module (Schedule 1). Sections 1.3 and 17.4 supersede the Term Sheet, so its narrower Section 7 does not cure the problem. The issue is still actionable. Nipusk's non-renewal notice of October 20, 2026 relied on the Term Sheet's 30-day window. Section 12.2 of the Agreement requires 90 days' notice, which meant by about October 2, 2026. Lusen may therefore argue the Agreement has renewed for a three-year Renewal Term, which would extend this exclusivity through 2029. Nipusk has not accepted any renewal and has expressly reserved its rights. The breadth of the covenant therefore remains a live exposure and a point to dispute or negotiate.

results.evidence: Section 12.2: "At the end of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall renew automatically for successive three-year Renewal Terms (each, a "Renewal Term"), unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term." Schedule 1, para 5: "At the start of each Renewal Term, the per-Vessel annual license fee in effect immediately before that Renewal Term increases by seven percent (7%)." Sections 1.3 and 17.4: "This Agreement supersedes the Term Sheet."
results.reason: The Term Sheet (s.5.2) agreed one-year renewals on 30 days' notice, and it was expressly non-binding on this point. The signed Agreement instead imposes three-year auto-renewal on 90 days' notice, plus a 7% fee uplift, and states twice that it supersedes the Term Sheet. The non-renewal notice obligation falls on Nipusk. For a December 31, 2026 expiry, the 90-day deadline was about October 2, 2026. Nipusk's letter is dated October 20, 2026 and relies expressly on the superseded 30-day Term Sheet period, so it is late under the Agreement. On the Agreement's terms, Nipusk now faces a three-year renewal through 2029 at 7% higher fees. This remains actionable rather than history. The folder shows no acceptance of renewal: no restated agreement and no payment of renewal fees. Nipusk's letter asserts non-renewal, reserves all rights, and states that continued use or payment is not agreement to renewal. Today (November 10, 2026) is before the Initial Term ends. Nipusk still needs advice on its exposure, its arguments and a negotiated exit before any Renewal Term begins.

results.evidence: Schedule 2, para 9: "This Schedule 2, and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with Vessel Data, is governed by and shall be construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales. Any such dispute or claim shall be referred to arbitration in London in accordance with the terms of the London Maritime Arbitrators Association..." Section 1.3: "If there is any conflict or inconsistency between the main body of this Agreement and any Schedule, the Schedule prevails over the main body." Section 15.1: "This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware... Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state or federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement."
results.reason: The conflict exists and still matters to Nipusk. Section 15.1 chooses Delaware law and the Wilmington courts, which matches the term sheet. Schedule 2 para 9 instead sends any dispute 'in connection with Vessel Data' to English law and LMAA arbitration. Vessel Data is defined very broadly: it covers AIS, noon reports, fuel, route, performance, emissions, charter-party particulars and all outputs derived from them. That means most operational disputes would fall within para 9. Section 1.3 gives the Schedules priority over the main body, so the English law and London arbitration choice would likely override Delaware for those disputes. Disputes could therefore be split between two forums. Nothing in the folder fixes this, and Nipusk has not accepted the result. The issue is live now. Nipusk's non-renewal letter relies on the term sheet's 30-day notice window, while the Agreement requires 90 days, so a renewal dispute is likely. That dispute also touches Nipusk's election on return of Vessel Data, which makes it uncertain which law and which forum would govern it.

results.evidence: Section 16.3: "Licensor may assign, transfer or novate this Agreement, in whole or in part, together with its rights in and to Vessel Data under Schedule 2, to any Permitted Transferee without the consent of or notice to Licensee." Section 1.1: "'Permitted Transferee' means any person, including any shipowner, ship operator or charterer, that acquires (by merger, purchase of equity or assets, or otherwise) all or any part of Licensor's business or assets, and any Affiliate of Licensor."
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable for Nipusk. Section 16.2 requires mutual consent for assignment but carves out Section 16.3. Section 16.3 lets Lusen assign the Agreement and its Vessel Data rights to a Permitted Transferee without consent or even notice. That definition expressly includes shipowners, operators and charterers, so it covers Nipusk's competitors. It also captures anyone buying "any part" of Lusen's assets. Vessel Data covers route, fuel, bunkering, cargo and charter-party particulars. Nipusk gets no reciprocal assignment right and no right to terminate on a change of control. Nothing in the folder cures this. The Term Sheet (s.10.3) contemplated mutual consent only, but Sections 1.3 and 17.4 say the Agreement supersedes it. The issue is still live. The Agreement runs at least to December 31, 2026. Nipusk's October 20, 2026 non-renewal letter relies on the Term Sheet's 30-day window, not the Agreement's 90-day notice requirement in Section 12.2. If that notice is ineffective, the Agreement may auto-renew for three more years. The exposure remains a real risk to raise and to renegotiate.

results.evidence: Letter ¶2.1: "This notice is given in accordance with the renewal terms agreed between the parties in the term sheet dated October 16, 2023 ... at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term." Letter ¶2.2: "This notice is given more than thirty (30) days before December 31, 2026." Agreement §12.2: "unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term." Agreement §§1.3 and 17.4: "This Agreement supersedes the Term Sheet."
results.reason: The Initial Term ends December 31, 2026 (§12.1), so the 90-day deadline under §12.2 was October 2, 2026. Nipusk's notice is dated and couriered October 20, 2026, 18 days late. The letter relies on the term sheet's 30-day period, but that term sheet was non-binding (TS §1.2) and the Agreement expressly supersedes it (§§1.3, 17.4). On the Agreement's terms, it therefore renews automatically for a three-year Renewal Term to December 31, 2029, with a 7% fee increase (Sched. 1 ¶5). The exclusivity in §3.4 would continue throughout that term. Nipusk bears the notice obligation and the late notice harms it. The problem is still actionable. Today is November 10, 2026, before the term ends. Nipusk has reserved its rights and disclaimed any renewal (¶¶4.1–4.2). Nothing in the folder shows it has paid renewal fees or otherwise accepted renewal. Counsel can still negotiate, look for other exit grounds, or prepare for a dispute.
